{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash -l

# Flux batch script
#
# Submit with (equivalent resources to Slurm directives):
#   flux batch -N 1 -n 8 -c 5 -g 8 -t 1d -o output=/jmain02/home/J2AD019/exk01/$USER/logs/%j.out ./openpsg.flux.sh <config>
#
# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=openpsg not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: job identification in listings/history may be less convenient, but runtime performance is unaffected.
#
# NOTE: Slurm --output=... uses %j (Slurm jobid) expansion, which Flux does not provide in a portable way via `-o output=...`.
# Performance implication: none; operational implication: you must ensure unique output paths yourself (otherwise logs may overwrite).

source ~/.bashrc
module load cuda

# In Flux, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is commonly set for the job step; this will reflect the step placement.
nvidia-smi -i "$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
nvcc --version

CONFIG=$1
GPUS=8
PORT=$(shuf -i 10000-65535 -n 1)

export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128

# Run 8 ranks (1 per GPU) within the Flux allocation.
PYTHONPATH="$(dirname "$0")/..":$PYTHONPATH \
EVAL_PAN_RELS=False \
WANDB_MODE="offline" \
flux run -n 8 -c 5 -g 8 \
  python -m torch.distributed.launch \
    --nproc_per_node=$GPUS \
    --master_port=$PORT \
    tools/train.py \
    $CONFIG \
    --auto-resume \
    --no-validate \
    --seed 666 \
    --launcher pytorch
"
}

If submitted/run without those flags, the job will get default resources and may not have 8 GPUs / 40 CPU cores available.

issues: Portability: requesting GPUs via `-g 8` assumes the site Flux instance is configured with GPU generic resources; otherwise submission or the step allocation can be rejected or remain unschedulable.

# Flux `-o output=...` does not portably expand %u (user) / %j (jobid).
# Performance implication: none; operational implication: without unique filenames, logs can overwrite.
#
# NOTE: Slurm --ntasks-per-node=8 is mapped to total tasks `-n 8` assuming 1 node (`-N 1`).
# Performance implication: none if you truly want 1 node; if multi-node was intended, adjust -N/-n.

source ~/.bashrc
module load cuda

nvidia-smi -i "$CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"
nvcc --version

CONFIG=$1
GPUS=8
PORT=$(shuf -i 10000-65535 -n 1)

export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128

# Run within the allocation granted by `flux batch`.
# Requesting explicit resources again here is optional; kept to preserve Slurm intent.
PYTHONPATH="$(dirname "$0")/..":$PYTHONPATH \
EVAL_PAN_RELS=False \
WANDB_MODE="offline" \
flux run -n 8 -c 5 -g 8 \
  python -m torch.distributed.launch \
    --nproc_per_node=$GPUS \
    --master_port=$PORT \
    tools/train.py \
    $CONFIG \
    --auto-resume \
    --no-validate \
    --seed 666 \
    --launcher pytorch

reasons: The script itself contains no Flux batch resource specification; the resource request (N=1, n=8, c=5, g=8, t=1d, output=...) is only provided in a comment. If submitted without those `flux batch` flags, Flux will allocate default resources and the job may not have the required CPUs/GPUs.

The `flux run -n 8 -c 5 -g 8` step requires the enclosing allocation to include at least 8 task slots, 40 CPU cores, and 8 GPUs; if the outer allocation is smaller (e.g., defaults), the step can be rejected or fail due to insufficient allocated resources.
issues: None specific to resources beyond the reliance on the submit command in the comment.
